title: /sessions/read carries each seat's provider and the agent CLI version it is running
description:
SPIDR prerequisite of task-c090faae9fbe438b959e76a08b7dcfdb (architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05), cut on the INTERFACE axis. That row is the browser PROOF row and its own rail 3 says "THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD" - but its DoD-1 requires Seats to show PROVIDER, CREDENTIAL SOURCE and CLI VERSION per seat, and two of those three do not exist to be proven. This row builds the missing production surface so the proof row can stay a proof row.

MEASURED AT HEAD f3b94eaa (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-b63fabf3, all three parts of DoD-1 checked separately:
- CREDENTIAL SOURCE: ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY SAFE. `apps/control-room/src/v2/resources/resources-credential.ts` is documented as "THE ONE PLACE THE PROVIDER'S CREDENTIAL IS TURNED INTO SOMETHING RENDERABLE", with a CLOSED grammar `credential/<leaf>/(env:<VAR>|login-file|ungated)`, a fail-closed `RESOURCES_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED`, and `credentialSourceWords()` for the operator's words. The ref is produced daemon-side by `activation-receipts-measure.ts:90` and already reaches the browser through `/activation/read` (`live-activation.ts`). NOTHING TO BUILD - this row does not touch it, and the proof row REUSES it rather than writing a second grammar (its own header warns against exactly that second scrub).
- PROVIDER: task-3958769c is adding `agentProvider: { effective, envOverride }` to /sessions/read, but that member is PROJECT-scoped - `createSessionsReadPort` takes `projectId` and no goal or seat. A PER-SEAT provider is a different member on `SessionView` (sessions-read.ts:49-58: capabilities, expiresAt, holding, liveness, principalId, sessionId, status) and does not exist.
- CLI VERSION: `git grep -rn '\-\-version' -- apps/daemon/src` finds NO probe for an agent CLI. Not built anywhere. `apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-version.node.ts:153-158` has a `runVersion(image, ["--version"])` helper that is the shape to reuse rather than invent.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: two new per-seat members on `SessionView` - the provider that seat is running under, and the agent CLI version it reported - measured daemon-side, plus the browser decoder moving in the SAME COMMIT.

THE EXACT-KEY TRAP, and it is why dependsOn is set: `SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS` and the per-seat decode in `apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts` are EXACT-ARITY. A member added on the daemon and not the decoder does not degrade the Seats screen, IT BLANKS IT. task-3958769c is moving the same frame; landing concurrently would collide. Wait for it, then move both halves together. Note also the cross-package SOURCE-TEXT pin at `live-sessions.test.ts:63-75`, which reads sessions-read.ts as text and matches top-level members with `/^ {2}readonly ([A-Za-z]+)[?]?:/gmu` - it pins the FRAME members, so a per-seat member sits outside it, but read that test before assuming.

A DESIGN QUESTION THE PLAN MUST SETTLE, NOT THE WORKER: a CLI version is a MEASURED fact about a child process the daemon does not own, and the daemon and wrapper are SEPARATE PROCESSES - sessions-read.ts:29-35 already documents that boundary for `configuredAgentLimit` ("CONFIGURED, never observed... Nothing here measures the wrapper"). Decide and record: is the version captured at SPAWN by the wrapper and written durably with the session, or probed by the daemon at read time? The first is honest and costs a durable write; the second cannot see a seat's actual binary. Whichever is chosen, the member's NAME must carry which kind of fact it is, exactly as `configuredAgentLimit` does.

NOT IN SCOPE: the Seats rendering, the toggle, any Playwright journey, the docs and the live drive - all task-c090faae's. The project-scoped `agentProvider` member - task-3958769c's. The credential-source grammar - already landed.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` AND `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (the decoder lives in apps/control-room and no other leg sees it).
definitionOfDone: `SessionView` (apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts) carries two new per-seat members: the provider that seat runs under, and the agent CLI version it reported. Both are MEASURED, and each member's NAME says what kind of fact it is - follow `configuredAgentLimit`'s precedent three lines away, whose docblock states "CONFIGURED, never observed" because the daemon and wrapper are separate processes. A name that implies observation the daemon cannot perform is a defect even when the value happens to be right.

The SPAWN-vs-READ decision is MADE, RECORDED and TESTED: state in the completion record whether the version is captured at spawn and written durably with the session, or probed at read time, and why. A test asserts the chosen path end to end - for the durable path, that a session written by one store instance reads back the version from another; for the probe path, that a probe failure degrades to a stated unknown rather than blanking the seat.

The browser decoder moves in the SAME COMMIT: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts` decodes both new per-seat members under exact-key rules. A test adding an extra key, dropping a key, or supplying a wrong-typed member on a SESSION returns ERROR `SESSIONS_RESPONSE_INVALID` at `CONTROL_ROOM_LIVE_SESSIONS` - assert the CODE AND THE LAYER. Type-guard a string with a non-empty check and never a truthiness test, the way the file already guards `record.unreadable` with `typeof x === "boolean"`.

A VERSION THE DAEMON DOES NOT KNOW IS STATED, NEVER GUESSED. A seat whose CLI version could not be measured renders a stated unknown, not an empty string and not a plausible default. Assert the unknown case explicitly; `demo-seed-payloads.ts:64` and `demo-seed-policy.ts:106` are the precedent in this repo for refusing to vouch for a `--version` reading nobody took, and both say so in those words.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: add the member to the daemon's `SessionView` only, leaving the decoder alone, and confirm a per-seat decode arm goes RED - not merely that a count changed. That drill is what proves the two halves must land together; the failure mode otherwise is a BLANK Seats screen rather than a red test. `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths first and say which restore proof applies to which path.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (MANDATORY - the decoder and its test live in apps/control-room and NO other leg sees them), `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for either package: vitest.config.ts:32 has no `apps/**` in its include.
taskRails: THE TWO HALVES LAND IN ONE COMMIT. The /sessions/read decoder is EXACT-ARITY: a daemon member without its decoder key does not degrade the Seats screen, it BLANKS it. Never land the daemon half alone, not even briefly.

NAME THE FACT FOR WHAT IT IS. The daemon and the wrapper are separate processes and the daemon cannot observe a child it did not spawn. `configuredAgentLimit` (sessions-read.ts:29-35) is the precedent: the limit of the claim lives in the NAME and in the docblock, not only in a comment somewhere else.

DO NOT REBUILD THE CREDENTIAL-SOURCE GRAMMAR. `apps/control-room/src/v2/resources/resources-credential.ts` already owns it, closed and fail-closed, and its header warns against a second scrub. This row adds no credential surface of any kind.
NEVER RENDER OR PUBLISH A CREDENTIAL VALUE. A version string is not a secret; a credential is. If a probe's output could contain one, do not publish the raw output.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: THE SPAWN-vs-READ DECISION, SETTLED: A SEAT-START RECORD, WRITTEN BY THE WRAPPER, ON THE PATTERN THIS DIRECTORY ALREADY USES. When I filed this row I named two options - widen `session.open` (durable but expensive) or probe at read time - and measurement found a better third. RECORD THIS REASONING IN THE STEP NOTE so a later worker does not re-open it. THE MEASUREMENT: `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/provider-pause-ledger.ts:113-152` `recordSeatExit` already writes ONE DURABLE RECORD PER SEAT, keyed by (projectId, sessionId), carrying `provider` among its fields - and `SEAT_EXIT_COMMAND_KIND` is `"internal.wrapper.seat_exit"` (provider-pause-contracts.ts:21) which appears ZERO times in daemon-command-vocabulary.ts. It is a DAEMON-INTERNAL ledger kind that commits straight to the store; it needs no PAYLOAD_KEYS entry, no registry entry, no MCP fence, no contracts roster and no generated client. So the durable path costs NONE of the roster work that made option (a) look expensive - widening `session.open`'s exact-arity payload `["capabilities", "credentialSha256", "expiresAt", "sessionId"]` was never the only way to be durable. WHY NOT THE READ-TIME PROBE: the daemon cannot see the binary a seat is actually running (separate processes), so a probe at read time measures the DAEMON's PATH and would publish it as if it were the seat's - the precise dishonesty `configuredAgentLimit`'s docblock exists to prevent. It would also run a child process on every Seats poll. BUILD IT: a seat-START record mirroring `recordSeatExit` line for line - mint a commandId, encode the result bytes, DECODE BEFORE COMMITTING (that file's own comment: "a record this module could not read back is never written"), commit to an aggregate keyed by (projectId, sessionId), and return the same replayed/conflict result shape. Carry the provider and the CLI version. Put it in a new module beside the pause ledger, or extend that one if it stays under 250 lines after the addition (it is 239 now, so a new module is the likely answer - measure and say which). THE VERSION PROBE: run `<command> --version` ONCE per wrapper process per distinct provider, never per spawn - a probe on every seat start adds child-process latency to the hot path. `apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-version.node.ts:130-162` is the shape to reuse: it returns null on any failure and falls through to a CODED UNKNOWN, with the comment "on a host where no non-shim pnpm resolves, 'I could not read it' is the correct and only honest answer". Copy that posture exactly - DoD-4 requires a stated unknown, never an empty string and never a plausible default.

NEW MODULE, NOT AN EXTENSION - measured as the plan asked: provider-pause-ledger.ts was 239 and is now 243 (only `existing`, `commit` and `CommitInput` were EXPORTED, +4 lines with the docblock). Three new modules instead:
  seat-start-contracts.ts 140 - the durable exact-key shape {agentVersion, projectId, provider, sessionId, startedAt, version}, `seatStartAggregateId`, an INPUT-DERIVED `seatStartRecordId` (so two wrapper processes replay one decision rather than writing two), `decodeSeatStartBytes`, `shapeAgentVersion`.

`commit`/`existing` are IMPORTED from provider-pause-ledger.ts, never copied: two wrapper-fact modules with two copies of the replay lookup is how one silently stops deduping.

THE PROBE - ONCE PER PROVIDER PER WRAPPER PROCESS, NEVER PER SPAWN. `createAgentVersionMemo` memoises the PROMISE keyed by the resolved command, so two simultaneous seats share one child instead of racing two, and a FAILED probe is memoised too (retrying a missing binary every spawn is the cost the memo exists to avoid, and the answer would not change). Bounded at `AGENT_VERSION_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` with maxBuffer 64KB and windowsHide.
IT RUNS THE COMMAND THE WAY THE SPAWNER DOES: `agentSpawnInvocation(command, ["--version"])` is REUSED, not re-derived. On Windows the CLI is a `.cmd` shim only a shell resolves, and that module already refuses any argument cmd.exe could reinterpret (`UNQUOTABLE`). A second resolution of the same name could measure a different image than the seat gets.

NEVER PUBLISH RAW PROBE STDOUT (task rail 4). `shapeAgentVersion` admits ONE non-empty line only (doctor-version.node.ts's posture: "Extra output means something else answered"), <= AGENT_VERSION_MAX_CHARS 96, matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ._()@/-]*$` AND containing `\d+\.\d+`. Everything else becomes the stated unknown. `decodeSeatStartBytes` RE-SHAPES on the way OUT too, so a row written by a looser build cannot publish what this one would refuse.

What you now have is MEASURED but SECOND-HAND: the wrapper measured it at spawn and wrote it down; the daemon is reading that record, not observing a live process. That is a different claim from `activeSeats` ("IS measured, from the same ledgers this read already folds") and a different claim from `configuredAgentLimit` ("CONFIGURED, never observed"), so do not borrow either word without thinking. Write the docblock in the file's own voice stating: which process measured it, WHEN, and what a reader may therefore conclude - specifically that a seat whose record predates a provider change still reports what it was actually started with, which is the useful answer, not a stale one. Decide what those report and make it the same stated unknown as a failed probe rather than a second vocabulary - one unknown, one meaning. Do NOT touch the frame-level `agentProvider` member: it is task-3958769c's and it answers a different question (what the PROJECT is set to, not what THIS seat is running).
implementationPlan.note:
THE TWO PER-SEAT MEMBERS ARE PUBLISHED. `SessionView` (sessions-read.ts) now carries `agentVersionAtStart` and `providerAtStart`.

THE NAMES CARRY THE LIMIT OF THE CLAIM (DoD-1). Both end in `AtStart` because these are a THIRD kind of fact, and the docblock says so in the file's own voice: `activeSeats` IS measured by this read from ledgers it folds itself; `configuredAgentLimit` is CONFIGURED and never observed; these two are MEASURED BUT SECOND-HAND - the WRAPPER measured them, in the wrapper's process, at the instant it spawned this seat's child, and wrote them down. This read is quoting that note. A bare `provider` or `agentVersion` would claim a present-tense observation nothing performs, and the daemon COULD not perform it: separate processes, and the daemon cannot see a child it did not spawn.

WHAT A READER MAY CONCLUDE, stated in the docblock: these say what the seat WAS ACTUALLY STARTED WITH, which is the useful answer and NOT a stale one. After `project.set_agent_provider` changes the setting, a seat running from before keeps reporting what it really runs while the frame-level `agentProvider` reports what the NEXT seat would get. THE TWO DISAGREEING IS THE DISCLOSURE WORKING - that window is exactly when an operator needs both. Also stated: nothing here re-probes, so a CLI upgraded on disk mid-run still reports the version its running process loaded.

THE THIRD LEDGER IS INJECTED WITH A DEFAULT, exactly as `readSessions` and `readClaims` are: `readSeatStarts?: (store, projectId) => SeatStartLedger`, defaulted to `readSeatStartLedger`. The port stays drivable without sqlite. A default cannot publish an untold value here the way a defaulted `configuredAgentLimit` would - absent notes ARE the fact the unknown states.

A SEAT WITH NO NOTE IS THE NORMAL CASE, NOT AN ERROR, and takes the SAME stated unknown as a failed probe: `seatStarts.get(record.sessionId) ?? SEAT_START_UNKNOWN`, both members `"UNKNOWN"`. Four causes collapse to that one token (no record - every session opened before this ledger existed and every paired browser that never had a seat; an unreadable record; a failed or timed-out probe; unshapeable output). One unknown, one meaning.
An undecodable seat-start row is SKIPPED by `readSeatStartLedger`, NOT escalated to the frame's `unreadable` flag: a corrupt note about which version a seat started with is not a reason to tell an operator the session ledger is broken. The pause ledger skips the same way.

`providerAtStart` uses the SAME naming rule as `agentProvider.configured` (roster leaf where known, verbatim where not), so the two members can never disagree about what to call one command.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: the frame-level `agentProvider` (task-3958769c's, and it answers a different question - what the PROJECT is set to, not what THIS seat is running), `concurrency` (task-92d84d38's), and the refusal shape (still exactly {code, layer, outcome}).

THE OPEN DESIGN QUESTION IS SETTLED, BY A THIRD OPTION I DID NOT NAME WHEN I FILED THIS ROW. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 6 steps, 6 files, 1 new.

I filed this row naming two options — capture at spawn and write durably, or probe at read time — and flagged the durable path as costing "a durable write". Measurement found a better third, and the plan settles it rather than passing the choice on.

## The measurement

`provider-pause-ledger.ts:113-152` `recordSeatExit` already writes **one durable record per seat**, keyed by `(projectId, sessionId)`, **already carrying `provider`**. And decisively:

```
provider-pause-contracts.ts:21   SEAT_EXIT_COMMAND_KIND = "internal.wrapper.seat_exit"
grep -c 'seat.exit\|seat_exit' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts   ->   0
```

It is a **daemon-internal ledger kind** that commits straight to the store. No PAYLOAD_KEYS entry, no registry entry, no MCP fence, no contracts roster, no generated client.

So a **seat-START record on that same pattern** is durable at *zero* roster cost. What made the durable path look expensive when I filed this was my assumption that it meant widening `session.open`'s payload — `["capabilities", "credentialSha256", "expiresAt", "sessionId"]`, exact arity, i.e. the full multi-file roster job. It does not.

**Read-time probing is rejected on the honesty ground the row was filed on:** the daemon cannot see the binary a seat is actually running — separate processes — so it would measure the *daemon's* PATH and publish it as the seat's. That is exactly what `configuredAgentLimit`'s docblock exists to prevent. It would also spawn a child process on every Seats poll.

The seat-EXIT record itself is not reusable for this: it is written at exit, so a **live** seat has none — and live seats are what Seats renders.

## Three things the plan pins that the description did not

1. **These members are a THIRD kind of fact.** Not `activeSeats` ("IS measured, from the same ledgers this read already folds") and not `configuredAgentLimit` ("CONFIGURED, never observed"). They are measured by the *wrapper* at spawn and read *second-hand* by the daemon from a ledger. Neither existing word is borrowable; the docblock must say which process measured it and when.

2. **A seat with no start record is NORMAL, not an error.** Every session opened before this row lands has none, and a paired browser session never had a seat at all. If that renders differently from a failed probe, an operator learns a distinction that does not exist — one unknown, one meaning.

3. **The guard boundary is not where you would assume.** `SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS` and the cross-package source-text pin at `live-sessions.test.ts:63-75` govern **top-level frame** members only. These are **per-seat**, decoded by `sessionOf(raw)` — so that pin does not cover them. Step 1 makes the worker confirm what *does* guard `sessionOf` and say so; a member unguarded on both sides is silent drift.

## Two safety notes on the probe

The probe takes its command from a **durable setting an operator can write**. `doctor-version.node.ts` guards the analogous case explicitly so "a version probe" cannot become "execute whatever the environment names" — read that guard first. And never publish raw probe stdout: clip and shape it, and say what you clip.

It must also be **once per wrapper process per distinct provider, never per spawn**, and bounded — a probe that hangs hangs the wrapper's startup.
